payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow designs. Independent auditing corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold; the earlier 12,000-cycle claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth of discharge. The battery has a gravimetric energy density of 148 Wh/kg, a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale, and an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C because the dopant precipitates at lower temperatures.
